summary: US tech bounced Monday (Nasdaq-100 +1.1%) on easing AI-credit worries, but the rally was narrow and Treasury yields jumped ~6bp to 5.15% as oil near $100 and Fed-hike pricing (~26bp by December) rose; the dollar firmed and USD/JPY climbed to ~158.5. No tier-1 events in the next 24 hours; Netflix reports after the US close.
events_next_24h: Tue 12:15pm CNY China loan prime rate (Oct)
Tue 5:00pm GBP UK unemployment / average earnings (Aug)
Wed ~7:00am USD Netflix earnings (after US close)

NKD.why: Nikkei closed -0.6% Monday and is ~6% off over five days, but the US tech bounce and weak yen help, and hedge funds are near a crowded short (12th pct).
NKD.risk: A second leg of the AI/chip sell-off or a sharp yen rally would turn it bearish.

NQ.why: Monday's +1.1% bounce only recovered part of Friday's -2% drop, and 5.15% 10-year yields plus a heavy earnings week (Netflix tonight) leave direction open.
NQ.risk: Strong megacap earnings and falling yields would make it bullish; renewed AI-credit fears bearish.

ES.why: S&P rose 0.4% on a few megacaps while the equal-weight index fell and decliners beat advancers ~2:1, as rising yields hit rate-sensitive sectors.
ES.risk: Broadening breadth with yields easing would flip it bullish.

YM.why: Dow was flat (-0.1%) with JPMorgan the main drag; no clear macro driver either way for the price-weighted index.
YM.risk: A further jump in yields or bank weakness would tilt it bearish.

RTY.why: Small caps held +0.25% despite yields rising to 5.15% and Fed-hike odds climbing, so the rate headwind and price action disagree.
RTY.risk: Another leg higher in yields or hike pricing would make it bearish.

6J.why: USD/JPY rose 0.4% to ~158.5 as the US-Japan yield gap widened and reports say the BOJ leans against an October hike.
6J.risk: Verbal or actual MoF intervention as USD/JPY nears 160, or hawkish BOJ guidance.

6E.why: EUR/USD slipped ~0.3% to 1.121 on French civil unrest and higher US yields supporting the dollar.
6E.risk: Calmer France, hawkish ECB speakers or a drop in US yields.

6B.why: Sterling dipped only ~0.1-0.2% on broad dollar strength, with UK jobs data today and UK CPI tomorrow able to swing it.
6B.risk: Hot UK wages or CPI would turn it bullish; weak data bearish.

6A.why: AUD outperformed Monday on firm China data and RBA's Kent questioning whether the 4.60% cash rate is restrictive enough.
6A.risk: Broad risk-off or a stronger US dollar would undo it.

ZN.why: 10-year yields rose ~6bp to 5.15% as oil-driven inflation worries and Fed-hike pricing (~26bp by December) both climbed.
ZN.risk: An Iran de-escalation that drops oil, or an equity sell-off driving a haven bid.

GC.why: Gold fell ~0.5% to ~$4,160 on higher yields and a firmer dollar, but Middle East risk and steady central-bank buying cushion it.
GC.risk: A further yield spike would make it bearish; Gulf escalation bullish.

CL.why: US easing of Russian energy sanctions and talk of an Iran breakthrough offset Houthi attacks and collapsing Hormuz tanker flows; November WTI expires today.
CL.risk: A confirmed Gulf supply hit (bullish) or an Iran de-escalation deal (bearish).
